README: GOLDEN FIXTURE — Scope 2 dual reporting (T5.3, CALC-5, TEST-3, О-11).
A FIXED set of energy rows, contractual instruments and factors, with the
expected MWh and kgCO2e for every one of them. Every number in an
`arithmetic` block was worked out BY HAND from the formulas of spec §9 —
not by running `computeScope2` and recording what it printed, which would
prove only that the code agrees with itself. The arithmetic IS the proof:
a reader can check any figure here with a pencil and no trust in the
implementation, exactly as in `scope1-basic.json`.
THE FACTOR VALUES ARE FIXTURE DATA, not the shipped `legacy-v1` set. The
grid values are DEFRA/AIB-shaped so the magnitudes read as plausible; the
residual-mix and supplier values are round on purpose, because the point of
this fixture is the MATCHING and a reader should not have to fight the
multiplication to check it. Note that `legacy-v1` carries NO residual-mix
rows at all today (see `RESIDUAL_MIX_ACTIVITY_TYPES` in `calc/scope2.ts`);
the ones here are what the set will look like once they are seeded, and the
`grid_average` fallback that stands in until then is exercised by the
district-heating row.
VERSION HISTORY OF THIS FILE. Written against hosmos-calc-1.1.0. The
version moved to 1.2.0 when the `supplier_specific` rung stopped admitting
any `source_name='supplier'` factor for any row naming any supplier and
started requiring the two to name the SAME seller (migration 0007 added
`emission_factor.supplier_name`). NOT ONE NUMBER BELOW CHANGED. The only
row the rung touches is ea05, whose supplier is `Zelena Energija d.o.o.`;
factor f5 was ALREADY that company's own product factor — it said so in
`factorName` prose, which no resolver can read — so the fixture now states
the same fact in the column the resolver matches on, and ea05's
market-based line is still 50 000 kWh x 0.100 = 5 000 kgCO2e. What WOULD
have moved, and is the defect 0007 closes: before the column existed, a
row naming ANY OTHER supplier was also priced by f5 at 0.100 instead of by
the residual mix at 0.500.
1.3.0 INSERTED A RUNG — unit distance, between geography and the
contextual/universal basis: a factor priced in the quantity the row was
ENTERED in (same unit, or one `unit_conversion` renames it onto at exactly
×1) beats any factor reached by a conversion that changes the number. It
DOES move shipped figures elsewhere (a `legacy-v1` gas bill in `kWh` used
to raise FACTORS_AMBIGUOUS and now resolves at ×1), so every line below
was re-checked against the new ladder. NOT ONE NUMBER BELOW CHANGED, and
the fixture makes the reason checkable with no code:
- `conversions` here is kWh↔MWh only, ×0.001 and ×1000. NEITHER is ×1,
so nothing is promoted to the `as_entered` rung by a renaming;
- EVERY factor f1…f6 is priced in `kWh`, so for any given row all its
candidates sit on the SAME distance rung — the MWh rows (ea01 ea02
ea04 ea05 ea06 ea08 eb01…eb04) are all `converted` through ×1000, the
kWh rows (ea03 ea07) are all the identity — and the rung therefore
ties everywhere and decides nothing. ea05, the one row with two
candidates (f1 the AIB grid average and f5 its own supplier's
product), is still decided by geography: `supplier_specific` outranks
`site_country`, exactly as before, and its market-based line is still
Only the version string moved here.
1.4.0 GAVE THE CONVERSION BASIS A SCOPE (migration 0010): a
`unit_conversion` row belonging to the period's PINNED factor set outranks
a shared one, contextual still beating universal inside each scope. It
moves shipped figures elsewhere — Slovenian gas in `kWh` under `si-2025`
used to reach ARSO's factors through DEFRA's UK calorific values, two
routes 3.69% apart that tied into FACTORS_AMBIGUOUS — so every line below
was re-checked. NOT ONE NUMBER BELOW CHANGED, and the fixture makes the
reason checkable with no code: BOTH conversions here carry
`"factorSetId": null` and are therefore shared rows, and the period pins
a set that owns no conversion of its own, so kWh↔MWh sits on the
`universal` rung exactly as before and every MWh figure is still
consumption × 0.001 or × 1000. Only the version string moved here.
WHAT THE FIXTURE COVERS, against the T5.3 acceptance:
- EVERY energy row yields EXACTLY TWO lines, one per `reporting_basis`
(К-20) — 8 rows in, 16 lines out;
- AC-5: ea06 is covered 100% by a GoO, so its market-based figure is 0
while its location-based figure is 28 800 kgCO2e;
- the 150% over-claim: e002's single instrument claims 300 MWh against
200 MWh of consumption, the matched volume is CAPPED at 200 and the
balance records `overClaimed: true` — which is what VAL-022 blocks on;
- the half-overlapping vintage: c104's window is 2024-07-04..2025-06-30,
exactly half of which lies in the period, so 200 MWh contributes 100;
- a vintage with NO overlap (c105, a 2023 certificate) contributes zero
and, just as importantly, adds zero to VAL-022's numerator;
- facility-bound BEFORE entity-level: c101 (bound to fa02) is sequence 0
and takes its bite `own_facility`, c102 (entity-level) is sequence 1;
- the balance closes: for every legal entity covered + residual =
consumption, on the nose (VAL-024);
- `location_factor_id` / `market_factor_id` are written back for all 8
rows (§4.10's Calculated fields) — including as NULL for the row that
could not be priced;
- the market-factor ladder, all three rungs: `supplier_specific` (ea05),
`residual_mix` (the SI and DE electricity rows) and `grid_average`
(ea07, district heating — no attribute market exists to strip);
- §0.7: ea08 sits in a country the set does not price and BOTH its lines
carry `failed_missing_factor` with a NULL result. Never a 0.
- CALC-1's four rejections, on both tables (eb01…eb04, cb01…cb02).
1.5.0 normalises factor output units to kgCO2e before final rounding.
Every factor here already outputs kgCO2e; all hand-worked numbers are unchanged.

The previous version of c102. Counting both would double the claim.

note: `supplier_product` is the one InstrumentType that is NOT a cancelled
attribute certificate: it names a product whose factor the supplier
publishes, and that factor may be anything. Pricing it at zero because
it arrived in this table would be §0.7's forbidden substitution in a
certificate's clothes. It reaches the calculation the other way — ea05
names the same supplier, and CALC-2's `supplier_specific` rung prices
the WHOLE of that row's remainder at 0.100 kgCO2e/kWh.

arithmetic: Entered in MWh, so the matching unit is reached by the identity and the
consumption is 400 MWh unchanged. c102 (entity-level, 500 MWh) reaches
this row first — the entity's rows are consumed in month order and
2025-03 precedes 2025-06 — and 400 is all it can take here:
Two instruments bite this row, in the order §9 fixes:
c101, bound to fa02 which IS this row's facility, takes 200 first;
c102 spills its remaining 500 − 400 = 100 onto it afterwards.
Entered in kWh, so CALC-3's universal row converts it for the matching:
c103 claims 300 MWh against it and gets 200 — THE CAP. The row cannot
be more than fully covered, so:
The 100 MWh c103 could not place is where VAL-022 comes from; see
`expectedEntities` for e002.
`year_month` is NULL — a whole-period row (DM-11), always inside the
window. Two instruments face it and only one lands anything:
c105 (2023 vintage) overlaps the period by 0 days → 0 MWh;
e004's only instrument is a `supplier_product`, which claims no volume
at all, so nothing is covered and the whole 50 MWh is the remainder —
priced by the supplier's own factor rather than by a residual mix.
AC-5. c107 covers exactly 120 MWh of exactly 120 MWh of consumption:
A residual of zero is what makes the market-based result zero below —
it is the ABSENCE of unmatched electricity, not a factor of zero found
in the set.
District heating. e005's GoO covers ELECTRICITY and cannot touch it:
the matching pool is the entity's electricity, per §9's denominator, so
40 000 kWh × 0.001 = 40.000 MWh, covered 0, residual 40.000000
Letting a certificate cover heat would understate a carrier nobody
bought a certificate for.
e006 holds no instruments, so the whole 10 MWh is residual. The volumes
are fine; it is the FACTOR that is missing (country ZZ), and the two
failures below are about that and nothing else.
SEQUENCE 0, AND THAT IS THE ASSERTION. c101 names fa02, c102 names no
facility, and §9 consumes facility-bound instruments first — so c101
sorts ahead of c102 whatever order the two arrived in.
Its window is the whole reporting year: 2025-01-01..2025-12-31 is 365
days and the overlap with the period is the same 365, so the volume
passes through UNPRORATED (no quotient is formed at all):
It is then offered fa02's rows before anything else, and ea02 has 600
MWh free, so the whole 200 lands there as `own_facility`.
Entity-level, so every allocation is `entity_spill` and the rows are
taken in month order:
ea01 (2025-03) is empty and has 400 MWh free → 400
ea02 (2025-06) has 600 − 200 (c101) = 400 free → the remaining 100
Note what the entity's total does NOT depend on: had c102 been consumed
first, it would have taken 400 from ea01 and 100 from ea02, and c101
would still have found 200 free at fa02. 700 MWh either way — the order
decides WHICH detail line carries the cover, never how much there is.
THE CAP, IN ONE INSTRUMENT. Full-year vintage, so 300 MWh is claimed in
full; e002 bought 200 MWh; ea03 therefore absorbs 200 and 100 MWh of
the claim has nowhere to go:
The matched figure is what the market-based arithmetic uses, which is
why no residual can go negative. The GAP between the two is what
VAL-022 reports — see e002 in `expectedEntities`.
A 2023 CERTIFICATE AGAINST A 2025 PERIOD. Its window
2023-01-01..2023-12-31 ends two years before the period begins, so
overlap = 0 days,  0/365 × 50 MWh = 0.000000
It covers nothing AND adds nothing to VAL-022's numerator — an
instrument that cannot be claimed is not an over-claim.
It is sequence 0 nevertheless, ahead of c104: both are entity-level, so
the tie-break is the vintage start and 2023-01-01 precedes 2024-07-04.
Being first costs nothing here because it has nothing to spend.
THE HALF-OVERLAPPING VINTAGE, and the window is picked so the halving
is exact and checkable rather than approximately a half.
the end of June, +4), and 2024 has 366 days, so
366 − 186 + 1 = 181 days of the window fall in 2024;
window = 181 + 181 = 362 days.
overlap with 2025-01-01 … 2025-12-31 = the 2025 half = 181 days.
prorated = 200 MWh × 181 ÷ 362 = 36 200 ÷ 362 = 100 EXACTLY
(check: 100 × 362 = 36 200 ✓; and 181/362 = 1/2, so the answer is
half of 200 by inspection as well)
The quotient is exact at 6 places, so `divideHalfUp` rounds nothing.
e003 consumes 300 MWh, so all 100 lands: matched = prorated.
AC-5's instrument: 120 MWh of full-year GoO against 120 MWh of
electricity. Everything is claimed, everything lands, and e005's
district-heating row is not touched because it is not electricity.
consumption = 400 (ea01) + 600 (ea02) = 1 000 MWh. The three excluded
rows carry 9 999 MWh each and CALC-1 keeps every one of them out.
claimed  = 200 (c101) + 500 (c102) = 700 MWh, both full-year vintages.
The two excluded certificates would have added 19 998 MWh.
covered  = 700 (nothing is capped: 700 ≤ 1 000)
residual = 1 000 − 700 = 300 MWh
THE 150% CASE, WHERE THE CAP AND THE RULE BOTH DO THEIR JOB.
consumption = 200 000 kWh × 0.001 = 200 MWh
claimed     = 300 MWh  (150% of 200)
covered     = 200 MWh  ← CAPPED at the consumption
residual    = 200 − 200 = 0 MWh
overClaimed = claimed > consumption = 300 > 200 = true → VAL-022 fails
WITHOUT THE CAP the residual would be 200 − 300 = −100 MWh and the
market-based figure −100 × 1000 × 0.620 = −62 000 kgCO2e — a negative
emission netting against real ones elsewhere in a total.
WITHOUT THE RULE the cap would swallow the 100 MWh of certificates that
cover nothing and the report would look perfect.
BALANCE (VAL-024): 200 + 0 = 200 ✓ — the balance closes BECAUSE of the
cap, which is exactly why the over-claim needs its own rule to surface.
consumption = 300 MWh (ea04, a whole-period row)
claimed  = 0 (c105, no overlap) + 100 (c104, half its window) = 100 MWh
covered  = 100, residual = 300 − 100 = 200 MWh
DECLARED RESIDUAL: c104 states `residual_mix_volume = 200`, and the
calculation computes 200. They agree, so VAL-024's second clause passes;
had the preparer typed 250 the rule would fail even though the engine's
own arithmetic balances — that contradiction is the point of the column.
The `supplier_product` claims no volume, so the entity claims nothing:
claimed = 0, covered = 0, residual = 50 − 0 = 50 MWh
BALANCE (VAL-024): 0 + 50 = 50 ✓
consumption counts ELECTRICITY only: 120 MWh (ea06). The 40 MWh of
district heating (ea07) is outside the balance entirely — it has its own
two lines and no certificate can reach it.
claimed = covered = 120, residual = 0.
100% covered, which is AC-5. BALANCE: 120 + 0 = 120 ✓
No instruments at all: claimed 0, covered 0, residual 10 MWh.
BALANCE: 0 + 10 = 10 ✓ — the VOLUMES balance perfectly even though
neither of this row's lines can be priced. The balance is about MWh; the
missing factor is a different failure with a different status.
The Slovenian grid factor is priced per kWh and the meter reads MWh, so
CALC-3's universal row multiplies by 1 000. No supplier is passed to
CALC-2 on this line by construction — a location-based figure a contract
could move would not be location-based.
400 MWh × 1 000 kWh/MWh = 400 000 kWh
half-up to 6 dp → 96000.000000
The row is fully covered by c102, so the UNMATCHED volume — which is
what a market-based line prices — is nothing:
The 400 covered MWh are priced at the certificate's zero and are absent
from `input_value` rather than multiplied by it, which is what keeps
`input × conversion × factor` re-derivable from the stored row.
Unmoved by the two certificates: location-based never sees them.
300 of the 600 MWh were covered (200 by c101, 100 by c102), so the
residual mix prices the other 300:
Above the location-based share of the same electricity, as a residual
mix should be: 0.500 > 0.240 because the certificates took the clean
attributes out of the pool.
A German site, so CALC-2 resolves the DE grid row — the site's country,
not the parent's. The meter reads kWh and the factor is priced per kWh,
so the conversion is the identity and no `unit_conversion` row is cited:
The over-claim, seen from the row. 300 MWh were claimed against 200 MWh
of consumption; the cap grants 200, so the residual is 0:
The row's market-based figure is legitimate ARITHMETIC and an illegitimate
CLAIM, and that is the whole reason VAL-022 exists beside the cap. Note
the line is still denominated in MWh while its location-based twin is in
kWh: the two prices two different quantities, the meter's and the
matching's.
The half-overlapping certificate covered 100 of the 300 MWh:
Had the vintage window been read as covering the period in full — the
mistake proration prevents — the covered volume would have been 200 MWh
and this figure 50 000, understating the market-based result by half.
The row names a supplier whose factor IS in the set, and the
location-based line still resolves the country grid: CALC-2's supplier
rung is unreachable unless the query names the supplier, and this query
does not.
THE TOP RUNG OF THE MARKET LADDER. The query names the supplier and
f5's `supplier_name` names the SAME seller, so that row for SI outranks
both the country grid and the residual mix, and the WHOLE remainder is
priced at it:
`method_code` follows the rung: `supplier_specific`, not `average_data`.
Nothing was covered by a certificate here — the entity's only instrument
is a `supplier_product`, which is evidence FOR this factor rather than a
volume claim, so it appears in `expectedSkippedInstruments` and its
50 MWh are matched by nobody.
AC-5, THE HALF THAT MUST NOT BE ZERO.
A guarantee of origin does not change the physics of the wire, so the
location-based figure is untouched by the 100% cover. A dual report
where BOTH figures went to zero would be the defect AC-5 is guarding
against.
AC-5, THE HALF THAT MUST BE ZERO.
This zero is a genuine one and is auditable: `coveredMwh` says 120 MWh
were covered, and `expectedMatches` names the certificate (c107) that
covered them. Contrast ea08 below, whose result is NULL — a figure
nobody could compute is never written as a 0 (§0.7).
District heating resolves the carrier's DEFAULT published factor, which
is GLOBAL rather than per country — the seed prices heat that way.
THE LAST RUNG. No supplier is named, and district heating has no
residual mix — there is no attribute market to strip out of it — so the
market-based line falls to the location-based factor and SAYS SO
(`marketFactorBasis: 'grid_average'`), which is what lets a renderer
avoid printing a market-based claim the data does not support.
IDENTICAL TO THE LOCATION-BASED FIGURE, and exactly so rather than
approximately: the two reached the same factor by different routes
(kWh × 1 and kWh × 0.001 × 1 000), and in exact decimal 0.001 × 1 000 is
1. In binary floating point it is not, and the two lines of the same
heat would disagree in the last place.
§0.7 / AC-6. The set prices SI and DE electricity and nothing else, so a
site in ZZ resolves NOTHING and the line carries no number at all — not
0, not '0.000000'. A zero here would sum into a total that looks
complete and reach a signed report unaudited.
All three rungs miss: the row names no supplier, ZZ has no residual mix
and ZZ has no grid average either. The VOLUME is perfectly well known —
`input_value` is the 10 MWh nothing covered — which is what makes this a
FACTOR failure and not a matching one. Both lines of the row fail, and
one failed line is enough to make the whole run `failed` (CALC-6).
LOCATION-BASED — the seven priced lines, summed as stored:
+   6 636   ea07 (district heating)
MARKET-BASED — the same seven rows, priced on what was NOT covered:
0   ea01 (fully covered)
+       0   ea03 (covered to the cap)
+   5 000   ea05 (supplier factor)
+   6 636   ea07 (no attribute market for heat)
Market-based below location-based (261 636 < 429 436) because 1 120 of
the 1 680 MWh of electricity carried certificates. ea08 contributes to
NEITHER total: it has no result at all, and its two failures are what
make the run `failed` and block approve, render and lock (CALC-6).
